titleEn: Indoor ag heavyweight 80 Acres Farms to cease operations
titleZh: 室内农业巨头80 Acres Farms宣布停止运营
summaryZh: 美国室内农业初创公司80 Acres Farms因无法获得继续运营所需资金而宣布停止运营。该公司曾运营5座全自动垂直农场，供应全美超18,000个零售点，累计融资超3.5亿美元，去年刚与Soli Organic合并。这是继Plenty、InFarm、Bowery等之后又一家倒闭的垂直农业公司，反映出该行业面临的资本困境。
featuredReason: 垂直农业与智慧畜牧同属农业科技赛道，其融资困境和商业模式挑战对畜牧业的自动化、设施化转型具有重要警示和借鉴意义。
contentFull:
US-based indoor farming startup 80 Acres Farms will cease operations, AgFunderNews has learned.

Cofounder and CEO Mike Zelkind noted in a statement that the company has been unable to secure the necessary capital to continue the business.

“After an exhaustive effort to find a way forward, 80 Acres Farms is winding down operations,” he said.

“For a decade, our team has proven that vertical farming can work at scale—building and operating indoor farms that ultimately supplied more than 18,000 retail locations across the US. We’re proud of our work, the problems we solved, and the fresh, clean produce that fed so many people.

“Unfortunately, under current circumstances, we could not secure the capital required to continue that work.

“We are deeply grateful to our employees, our retail partners, and the communities that have supported us. We have seen vertical farming’s potential up close, and we still believe that this industry is just getting started, and that we have helped plant the seeds for generations of future harvests.”

One of ‘world’s largest and most advanced’ vertical farming networks

Founded in 2015, Ohio-based 80 Acres Farms was operating five fully automated indoor vertical farms at its peak. Notably, these farms were powered with renewable energy, which addressed one of the major cost hurdles associated with vertical farming.

The company has raised more than $350 million, and last year merged with Soli Organic to create what the companies then called “one of the world’s largest and most advanced indoor farming networks.”

“We’re strong believers that this industry is necessary,” Zelkind said at the time. “The question is when and who, not when and if will happen. I hope this is the start of a new era.”

News of the closure follows a long list of vertical farming companies that have shuttered since 2022, including Plenty, InFarm, Bowery, and many others.

80 Acres has declined to comment any further at this time. AgFunderNews will update this post as more details emerge.

translationZh:
总部位于美国的室内农业初创公司80 Acres Farms将停止运营，AgFunderNews已获悉此事。

联合创始人兼首席执行官Mike Zelkind在一份声明中指出，公司未能获得继续经营所需的必要资金。

“在经历了寻找出路的竭尽全力之后，80 Acres Farms正在逐步停止运营，”他说。

“十年来，我们的团队证明了垂直农业可以规模化运作——我们建造并运营的室内农场最终为全美超过18,000个零售点供货。我们为我们的工作、我们解决的问题以及为众多人提供的新鲜洁净农产品感到自豪。

“不幸的是，在当前情况下，我们无法获得继续这项工作所需的资金。

“我们深深感谢我们的员工、零售合作伙伴以及一直支持我们的社区。我们近距离见证了垂直农业的潜力，我们仍然相信这个行业才刚刚起步，我们已经帮助播下了未来世代丰收的种子。”

**全球‘最大、最先进’的垂直农业网络之一**

80 Acres Farms成立于2015年，总部位于俄亥俄州，在巅峰时期运营着五座全自动室内垂直农场。值得注意的是，这些农场使用可再生能源供电，解决了垂直农业面临的重大成本障碍之一。

该公司已融资超过3.5亿美元，去年与Soli Organic合并，打造了当时两家公司所称的“全球最大、最先进的室内农业网络之一”。

“我们坚信这个行业是必要的，”Zelkind当时表示。“问题在于何时以及由谁来实现，而不是会不会实现。我希望这是一个新时代的开端。”

关闭的消息紧随自2022年以来一系列垂直农业公司倒闭的浪潮，包括Plenty、InFarm、Bowery等众多公司。

80 Acres目前拒绝进一步置评。AgFunderNews将在更多细节浮出水面时更新此报道。
author: Jennifer Marston
